raw_case_text:
A 56 years-old diabetic patient was admitted in February 2021 in ICU for a severe COVID-19 which required immediate mechanical ventilation. The patient received 10 days dexamethasone associated with two doses of tocilizumab according to the local standard of care protocol. One week after ICU admission, COVID-associated pulmonary aspergillosis was diagnosed based on the growth of Aspergillus flavus in broncho-alveolar fluid (BAL) culture, positive galactomannan both in BAL (index: 5.9) and in serum (index: 1.9) and new pulmonary infiltrates (Figure 1A). Voriconazole was started. A month later, abnormal neurological examination after sedation interruption led to the discovery of two brain abscesses associated with ethmoidal sinusitis (Figure 1B). ENT surgery was performed revealing bilateral extensive necrosis of sinonasal mucosa, maxillary and ethmoidal bone. Pathological tissues were respectively removed and drilled until reaching healthy hemorrhagic tissue. A transethmoidal roof procedure allowed for the drainage of the most anterior abscess. Rhizopus & Mucor PCR was positive in blood as well as in most of per-operative sinus and cerebral samples (Figure 1C). Pathology showed aseptate, broad-angled hyphae in the skull bones. Liposomal amphotericin B (L-AmB) was added and voriconazole was switched for isavuconazole when the diagnosis of cerebral mucormycosis was confirmed. Unfortunately, additional debridement was not feasible due to the vicinity of cerebral vessels and brain parenchyma. After ten days of dual antifungal therapy, the patient's condition worsened as the size of the non-drained abscess increased. Of note, the neutrophils level varied between 4.5 and 12 G/L.
At this step we analyzed by flow cytometry circulating T cells. The total T cell count was normal (1624/mm3) but the CD4/CD8 ratio was below 1 (CD4 = 557/mm3). Major lymphocyte subsets were further characterized by their expression of activation/differentiation markers and immune checkpoint molecules. The CD8+ T cell count was increased (CD8 = 938/mm3), and 60% of CD8+ T cells co-expressed CD38 and HLA-DR, that are late activation markers. CD4+ T cell expressed also high levels of HLA-DR (33%). Furthermore both CD8+ and CD4+ T cells expressed high levels of programmed cell death-1 (PD-1, 56% and 70%), an immune checkpoint molecule that has been associated with T-cell exhaustion. We also measured Aspergillosis and SARS-CoV-2 specific memory T cells using IFN-gamma ELISpot assay. We detected SARS-CoV-2 but no Aspergillus specific T cells in peripheral blood.
Because of the poor prognosis and high percentage of PD-1-expressing circulating CD4 and CD8 T-cells, immunoadjuvant therapy with IFN-gamma and nivolumab was started. The patient received 100 mg of interferon-gamma SC 3 times a week during a month and 2 IV injections of nivolumab 240 mg (3 mg/kg) four weeks apart. After two weeks of this treatment, the percentage of circulating CD4+ and CD8+ T cells expressing PD-1 substantially decreased, percentage that remained steadily low afterward (Figure 1D). After 3 weeks of immunoadjuvant therapy, an increase in CD4 T cells activation (as shown by the rise of CD4 T cells percentage expressing HLA DR) and CD8 T cells proliferative capacity (as indicated by the 4-fold increase of Ki67 expression) were observed (Figure 1D). Still, no Aspergillus specific T cells could be detected using IFN-gamma ELISpot assay. Under combined immunoadjuvant and dual antifungal therapy, the cerebral abscesses decreased in size and serum galactomannan and Mucorales PCR turned negative (Figures 1B, C).
Unfortunately, after one month the patient developed septic shock following ventilation acquired pneumonia with oliguric renal failure and hepatic cytolysis. L-AmB and IFN gamma were stopped and the patient remained under isavuconazole only. Despite several antibiotics and a good monitoring of isavuconazole residual concentration (between 3.1 and 4.2 mg/L) the patient's condition deteriorated. The size and number of cerebral abscesses increased and the Mucorales PCR was found positive in the CSF. After multidisciplinary concertation, palliative care was started, and the patient died 17 weeks after his initial hospitalization.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 56-year-old diabetic patient mechanically ventilated for severe COVID-19 developed COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis 1 week after ICU admission, followed 1 month later by abnormal awakening neurological examination from sinonasal and cerebral mucormycosis.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Admitted to the ICU in February 2021 for mechanically ventilated severe COVID-19 pneumonia and treated with 10 days of dexamethasone and two doses of tocilizumab, the patient developed pulmonary Aspergillus flavus infection on ICU day 7 (treated with voriconazole). One month after ICU admission, failure to awaken properly upon sedation interruption led to the discovery of ethmoidal sinusitis and two bifrontal brain abscesses caused by invasive rhino-orbito-cerebral mucormycosis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Diabetes mellitus; severe COVID-19 pneumonia treated with dexamethasone (10 days) and tocilizumab (2 doses).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for severe hypoxemic respiratory failure and subsequent persistent coma/abnormal neurological exam upon sedation weaning.

objective.physical_examination: Mechanically ventilated; abnormal neurological examination after sedation interruption at 1 month. Intraoperative ENT endoscopy revealed extensive bilateral necrosis of the sinonasal mucosa and maxillary and ethmoidal bones.
objective.routine_investigations: Neutrophil counts remained preserved between 4.5 and 12 G/L. Immune profiling at 1 month showed normal total T-cell count (1,624/mm3) with an inverted CD4/CD8 ratio <1 (CD4+ 557/mm3, CD8+ 938/mm3), marked T-cell activation (60% CD38+HLA-DR+ CD8+ T cells, 33% HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cells), and profound PD-1 exhaustion marker expression (56% of CD8+ and 70% of CD4+ T cells; reversing after nivolumab/IFN-gamma with a 4-fold rise in CD8+ Ki-67 proliferation), while IFN-gamma ELISpot detected SARS-CoV-2-specific T cells but zero Aspergillus-specific memory T cells.
objective.advanced_workup: At week 1, chest CT showed new pulmonary infiltrates, BAL culture grew Aspergillus flavus, and galactomannan was positive in both BAL (index 5.9) and serum (index 1.9). At 1 month, cranial MRI demonstrated ethmoidal sinusitis and two frontal brain abscesses. Skull-base bone histopathology from endoscopic transethmoidal debridement and anterior brain abscess drainage revealed broad, wide-angle aseptate hyphae, and Rhizopus/Mucor PCR was positive in peripheral blood, intraoperative sinus and cerebral samples, and later terminal CSF.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: COVID-19-associated pulmonary aspergillosis (Aspergillus flavus; confirmed by BAL culture and positive BAL [5.9] and serum [1.9] galactomannan) followed by fatal rhino-ethmoido-cerebral mucormycosis (confirmed by skull bone pathology showing broad aseptate hyphae and positive blood, sinus, brain, and CSF Rhizopus/Mucor PCR) in a diabetic patient treated with dexamethasone and tocilizumab. Treated with endoscopic sinonasal and transethmoidal anterior brain abscess drainage, switch from voriconazole to dual liposomal amphotericin B plus TDM-guided isavuconazole (troughs 3.1-4.2 mg/L), and salvage immunoadjuvant therapy with subcutaneous interferon-gamma (100 ug 3x/week for 1 month) plus IV nivolumab (240 mg q4w x 2 doses), which reversed T-cell PD-1 exhaustion, cleared serum galactomannan and blood Mucorales PCR, and shrank the brain abscesses; however, subsequent ventilator-associated pneumonia with septic shock, oliguric AKI, and hepatic cytolysis forced discontinuation of L-AmB and IFN-gamma, leading to CNS mucormycosis relapse and death at week 17.
